title: Client Bootcamp: Lightning Track — manifest & quicklabs (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, 90-minute hands-on "lightning" bootcamp to take a new integrator from signup -> sample app -> basic instrumentation. Focus: low friction, observable success signals, and clear fallback/next-step guidance. This doc is a delivery manifest for customer-facing workshops and internal quicklabs that product/SEs can run.

Core learning objectives:
- Make the first SDK call (any language) and stream a response within 15 minutes.
- Observe request/response in Console and capture token/cost telemetry.
- Wire a simple retry + fallback to a cheaper model variant.
- Create an embedding and perform a naive similarity lookup (mini RAG).
- Know where to look when things go wrong (latency, quota, auth).

Audience & prerequisites:
- Audience: Product engineers with HTTP/JS/Go/Python experience, limited LLM background.
- Prereqs we ask the customer to do ahead of time: create account, confirm org, add API key to a safe file, open their laptop with code editor.

Agenda (90 minutes total):
- 0-10m: Kickoff + expectations (what success looks like for the session). Quick show of Console.
- 10-25m: Quickstart lab — JS snippet to call /chat.stream and render to console. Validate streaming.
- 25-40m: Instrumentation lab — enable request-level telemetry, inspect token breakdown and latency chart.
- 40-60m: Resilience lab — implement retry with exponential backoff and fallback to a smaller model variant.
- 60-75m: RAG micro-lab — create embeddings for 3 docs, simple vector search, answer a query.
- 75-85m: Troubleshooting lightning — guided checklist for common failures.
- 85-90m: Next steps & handoff (dedicated/DVP options, SDK deep dives).

Quicklabs (step-by-step blurbs to paste into workshop slides):
1) Hello stream (JS, 10 lines) — paste snippet that sets API_KEY, calls chat stream, prints tokens as they arrive.
2) Token inspector (Python) — run a single request with debug headers on, parse the response metadata from Console, note prompt vs completion token counts.
3) Fallback demo (Go) — call expensive model, if 503 or >500ms tail latency, call small-model variant with same prompt; compare cost estimate.
4) Embedding + naive vector store (JS) — embed 3 short docs, simple cosine function, return top-1 and prompt model with that context.

Pre-built artifacts for facilitators (links to share during bootcamp):
- Lightweight repo with four folders: /js, /py, /go, /notebooks. Each folder contains a single working example and a smoke-test script.
- Console saved-query showing last 30 requests and token breakdown.
- Gist: 'retry + fallback' example generalized to any SDK.

Instrumentation & success signals to show during session:
- Request appears in Console within ~2 seconds of sending.
- Token cost shown per-request; highlight prompt vs completion ratio.
- One successful embedding query with match score >0.7 shown in notebook.
- Retry fires and logs when simulated 502 induced by local proxy.

Facilitator playbook notes (short):
- Have demo tokens/keys preloaded in environment variables for speed.
- If streaming fails, switch to non-stream sample to show core API contract.
- For slow customers, scale down to 45-minute core path: Hello stream + Token inspector + fallback.

Troubleshooting matrix (common cases & quick remedies):
- Auth error 401: check API key present and not expired; confirm org on Console.
- 429 rate limit: recommend using a short demo key with reduced concurrency; show Console rate-limiter panel.
- High token cost surprise: show how to inspect prompt template and trim system/preamble.
- Embeddings low quality: check input text length, dedupe stopwords, demonstrate paraphrase test.

Post-workshop checklist for attendees (email template bullets):
- 1) Add your API key to the secrets manager for your demo app.
- 2) Pin the model variant you used (or create a rollout policy).
- 3) Add token-level logging to your app; send one sample request per env to the Console.
- 4) Open a ticket with SE for dedicated capacity if throughput needs are >50 qps.

Notes for SDK team (actionable improvements surfaced during pilots):
- Provide a single-file "stream-only" sample for each language with no dependencies.
- Ship a tiny CLI that runs the smoke tests and prints token breakdown.
- Add a small UI tile in Console that highlights "first 3 requests" telemetry for new orgs.

Open questions / To-do (for product & docs):
- Should the bootcamp offer an offline / VPC variant hands-on? (ask private-deployments team)
- Create a short video walkthrough (3–4 min) for pre-read to cut live time.
- Decide standard model variants to recommend for demo (cost vs latency).

Appendix: sample quick-check commands (copyable)
- JS stream (node): export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx; node demos/js/stream.js
- Python token inspect: python demos/py/token_inspect.py --debug
- Quick embedding smoke: node demos/js/embed_smoke.js "Three facts about Redwood"

End of manifest — this is intentionally minimal and designed to be iterated. Use after-action notes from the first three customer bootcamps to create a permanent facilitator guide and a trimmed 45-minute variant.
